actions.description: Move the hexapod to a six-component pose and return the pose read after the controller reports STOPPED

inputs.description: Six-component SmarPod pose in the vendor API's own units: position X, Y, Z then rotation X, Y, Z, the order of SmarPod.pose_to_double_list (src/SmarPodMain.py:45-53). The clone states no unit; '1' is a placeholder, not a dimensionless claim, and one site envelope bounds all six components.

actions.description: Stop all motion on the resource with a declared deceleration profile and report the stopping position. This capability is always cancellable=false and is exempt from rate limiting.

device.model: SmarPod six-axis hexapod (the upstream class opens model 10052)
device.name: SmarAct SmarPod hexapod (gh.bsh90/smarpod-ophyd SmarSignal)

facts.text: SmarSignalRO derives from ophyd Signal, creates a SmarPod and opens the controller in its constructor
SmarSignalRO.get reads the current pose with smarpod.GetPose and returns pose_to_double_list(pose)
pose_to_double_list returns positionX, positionY, positionZ, rotationX, rotationY, rotationZ in that order
SmarSignal.set verifies reachability, calls smarpod.Move(handle, pose, 0, True) and then requires the move status to be stopped
SmarSignal.get_status reports stopped when smarpod.GetMoveStatus equals MoveStatus.STOPPED
SmarSignal.check_pose asks smarpod.IsPoseReachable; verify_reachable_position raises when it is not reachable
SmarSignalDifferentAxis.set constructs a new SmarSignalRO without an optional_handle, reads its pose, replaces component i and sets the pose through a new SmarSignal on that handle
SmarSignalRO.trigger reads GetMoveStatus once, before its loop, then sleeps 10 s per iteration while that single reading is not STOPPED; the loop never reads the status again
SmarPod.set_speed_and_frequency_and_pivot_point_and_coordinate_system sets speed, maximum frequency, RELATIVE pivot mode with pivot [10e-3, 0, 0] and a coordinate system
The SmarPod class attributes are model 10052 and locator usb:sn:MCS2-00006657

SmarPod.set_up opens the controller with its model and locator, calibrates, searches reference marks when the controller is not referenced, enables the sensor, then calls smarpod.Stop and raises when the move status is not STOPPED
The except clause of set_up catches smarpod.Error and Exception, logs and prints a message built from err.func and err.code, and does not re-raise
The stop path is smarpod.Stop(handle) followed by a fresh GetMoveStatus check for MoveStatus.STOPPED
SmarPod.moving checks every pose with IsPoseReachable and move_sequence sends each pose with smarpod.Move
The README describes connecting to a SmarPod through the Ophyd interface or directly to its API and states no pose unit, travel range or workspace bound
